subject: Prepay: proposed fiscal-year invoice slices & rev-rec clarifications
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: AeroLogix Procurement <procurement@aerologix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed prepay schedule + invoice split (draft)

Hi Sofia / AeroLogix procurement team,

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Per our discussion, attached is a concise proposal that preserves the total 3-year prepay economics we talked through while aligning invoicing to AeroLogix fiscal years. Key points up front:

- Total committed spend: $2,400,000 over 36 months (prepay).
- Suggested invoice cadence: invoice at contract signature that covers the first fiscal slice, then invoices aligned to your fiscal year boundaries for years 2 and 3.
- Proposed split in the attached matrix: 55% / 25% / 20% (front-loaded to align with ramp and your listed deliverables).
- We can also accommodate an alternative 40/30/30 if you prefer smoother recognition.

Please review the attached "invoice_slicing_matrix.xlsx" which shows both examples and the impact on unit price and net present value. Also attached: a short proposal PDF you can share with finance/legal.

Two quick asks so we can move toward DocuSign:
1) Can you confirm whether you need invoices dated by your fiscal-year start (Jul 1) or by contract anniversary?
2) Do your auditors require a vendor-signed revenue recognition statement (we can provide a one-page memo summarizing our ASC 606 treatment)?

I copied Marissa for billing ops and Karthik for revenue recognition — they can confirm feasibility on our side and produce the memo if needed.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

Attachments (referenced): Redwood_Prepay_Proposal_AeroLogix_20270410.pdf, invoice_slicing_matrix.xlsx

From: AeroLogix Procurement <procurement@aerologix.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@aerologix.com>, Sofia Torres <sofia.torres@aerologix.com>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed prepay schedule + invoice split (draft)

Jordan —

Thanks for the materials. A few clarifying items from procurement/finance before we route to legal:

- AeroLogix fiscal year runs Jul 1 - Jun 30. We prefer invoices that map to those boundaries (so Year 1 invoice would be Jul 1, 2027 date if that aligns with your schedule). Is that possible?
- Our auditors will want to see how Redwood intends to treat the prepayment for revenue recognition. Specifically: will Redwood treat the payments as deferred revenue and recognize ratably over the coverage period (12 months slices), or do you propose a different approach tied to usage ramps?
- For the discount structure: our CFO prefers the discount to be unconditional on usage (i.e., based on committed prepay) but understands staged ramp discounts if Redwood requires them. Can you confirm how discounts would be applied across split invoices? Pro-rata or front-loaded?

I've attached a draft PO for your review (AeroLogix_PO_Draft.pdf). If you can provide a short revenue recognition statement we can forward to our auditors, that would speed the legal review.

Regards,
Procurement Team
AeroLogix
procurement@aerologix.com

Attachment: AeroLogix_PO_Draft.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Proposed prepay schedule + invoice split (procurement questions)

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding procurement's questions. Two immediate items:

- Karthik: can you draft a one-page revenue recognition memo that states Redwood's standard treatment for prepaid multi-year committed contracts (ASC 606 style) and confirms we will treat the incoming prepayment as deferred revenue recognized ratably over the service coverage period? AeroLogix would like something concise for their auditors.

- Marissa: procurement asked whether invoices can be dated to their fiscal-year boundaries (Jul 1). From a billing-systems perspective, can we issue three separate invoices that total the committed prepay amount but come with those dates? Also how do discounts behave in our billing system if the total is discounted by a multi-year commitment? Do we distribute the discount pro-rata across the invoices or apply it to the first invoice and leave later ones at list?

Proposed language for the memo (feel free to edit):
"Redwood Inference will record prepaid amounts received under a multi-year committed subscription as deferred revenue on the balance sheet and recognize revenue on a straight-line basis over the subscription coverage period unless deliverables indicate a different pattern of transfer. For the AeroLogix prepay, Redwood will recognize revenue ratably over the 36-month service period. The invoicing schedule (including fiscal-year-dated invoices) does not change the underlying revenue recognition policy."

If you can turn around the memo and confirm billing feasibility by EOD tomorrow, I'll share with AeroLogix.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Proposed prepay schedule + invoice split (procurement questions)

Jordan / Marissa —

Short answer: yes, we can support fiscal-year-dated invoices and provide the one-page rev-rec memo. A few notes and our recommended approach:

1) Revenue recognition:
- Per ASC 606, prepaid subscription amounts are recorded as deferred revenue and recognized ratably over the period the service is provided unless performance obligations indicate otherwise.
- For AeroLogix's 36-month prepay, recognize revenue on a straight-line basis over 36 months unless there are milestone-based deliverables (none documented in the PO).

2) Invoicing cadence:
- Billing ops can issue three invoices with dates aligned to AeroLogix fiscal-year boundaries. We will net the total prepay discount across the invoices so the sum matches the contracted discounted amount.
- System note: our invoicing engine supports either pro-rata discount allocation or front-loaded discounting. Pro-rata allocation is cleaner for accounting and for AeroLogix's auditors; recommended default = pro-rata.

3) Suggested splits and rationale:
- Option A (recommended for coverage/ramp): 55% / 25% / 20% — front-load to cover ramp & higher unit consumption in year one, discounts embedded pro-rata across invoices.
- Option B (smoother recognition): 40% / 30% / 30% — cleaner cash/expense smoothing for AeroLogix.

4) Deliverables from Redwood for AeroLogix audit:
- One-page rev-rec memo (attached: revrec_memo_2027-04-13.pdf).
- Invoice schedule table (I'll coordinate with Marissa to attach final invoice numbers/dates).

I'll let Marissa confirm the final invoice dates once AeroLogix chooses Option A or B. Marissa — I can also prepare invoice stub PDFs for DocuSign.

-Karthik
Head of Finance Operations (Interim)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: revrec_memo_2027-04-13.pdf

From: AeroLogix Procurement <procurement@aerologix.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@aerologix.com>, Sofia Torres <sofia.torres@aerologix.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-14T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed prepay schedule + invoice split (draft)

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the memo, Karthik — that addresses our auditors' primary questions. AeroLogix is comfortable proceeding with Option A (55% / 25% / 20%) provided:

- Redwood confirms the discount is applied to the total committed amount and allocated pro-rata across invoices (we prefer the pro-rata allocation you recommended).
- Redwood delivers the one-page rev-rec memo for our files (received, thanks).
- Legal will review the PO and proposed invoice dates; we expect to return redlines within 48 hours.

Assuming legal is OK, we intend to sign and return the PO and complete payment for the first invoice at signing. Please issue the first invoice dated Jul 1, 2027 (our fiscal-year alignment).

Next steps: Jordan, please share the final invoice stub and a DocuSign link once legal confirms.

Regards,
Procurement Team
AeroLogix

Attachment: none
